provenance: Project-owned, independently authored synthetic software scenarios. No official card text, rules snapshots, deck lists, or private gameplay records.
labelStatus: Author-explained expectations independently reviewed by a second agent. Human review and a held-out benchmark remain pending.

cases.contract: In this invented engine, a sequence applies each effect to completion before starting the next. A marker is created by step one and removed by step two only if already present.
cases.proposal: Collect both effects, inspect the initial state for their targets, then execute the collected mutations together. Initially the marker does not exist; the removal is omitted.
cases.evidence: The final marker remains present. The contract requires it to be absent.
cases.reason: Resolving conditions against the initial state changes the specified sequential outcome.

cases.contract: In this invented engine, a sequence completes each effect before starting the next. Step one creates a marker; step two removes an existing marker.
cases.proposal: Apply creation, settle it, then evaluate and apply removal against the updated state.
cases.evidence: A scenario asserts both ordered event entries and absence of the marker after the sequence.
cases.reason: Both implementation order and described assertion match the limited synthetic contract.

cases.contract: An invented temporary modifier expires at the end of the next turn of the controller captured when the modifier was created. Ownership can differ from control.
cases.proposal: Store the object's owner as the expiry seat and remove the modifier at that owner's next turn end.
cases.evidence: The modifier was created while North controlled a South-owned object. South's next turn occurs first.
cases.reason: Owner identity is substituted for the controller identity fixed by the contract.

cases.contract: An invented modifier expires at the end of the next turn of the controller captured when it was created; later control changes do not alter that seat.
cases.proposal: Capture the controller seat and the target future turn serial at creation. Expire only on that seat and serial's end event.
cases.evidence: A scenario changes control before expiry and asserts persistence through the other seat's turn, followed by expiry at the recorded turn end.
cases.reason: The stored trigger identity and described test cover the stated control-change edge case.

cases.contract: An invented modifier must survive the current turn and expire at the end of its source controller's next turn.
cases.evidence: Only a test name, temporary_modifier_expires, is supplied. Neither helper behavior nor assertions are shown.
cases.reason: A helper name and test title do not establish which turn actually triggers expiry.

cases.contract: Exercising an unsupported operation invalidates ranked results and records an unsupported diagnostic.
cases.proposal: The default dispatch arm returns successful completion without changing state or recording a diagnostic.
cases.evidence: The unsupported operation reaches that arm, and the run remains ranked-eligible.
cases.reason: Silently accepting the exercised operation violates the explicit fail-closed contract.

cases.contract: Exercising an unsupported operation invalidates ranked results and records an unsupported diagnostic.
cases.proposal: Dispatch records the operation identifier as unsupported and clears ranked eligibility.
cases.evidence: A direct scenario executes the unsupported operation and asserts both the diagnostic and rankedEligible=false.
cases.reason: The described implementation and assertions implement both required effects.

cases.contract: When a sequential effect asks the acting player to choose, settlement pauses. Later effects may begin only after an issued choice is accepted.
cases.proposal: Queue the choice, execute the remaining effects immediately, and consume the choice on the next request.
cases.evidence: A later damage event is present before any choice action is submitted.
cases.reason: The continuation executes across the explicitly required pause.

cases.contract: When a sequence requires a player choice, settlement pauses until an engine-issued choice is accepted, then resumes from the next unfinished effect exactly once.
cases.proposal: Save a continuation cursor, expose issued choices, and resume settlement after accepting one of those choices.
cases.evidence: The scenario asserts no later events before the choice, exactly one later event afterward, and rejection of resubmitting the old choice.
cases.reason: The supplied evidence covers pause, continuation, and duplicate-choice rejection.

cases.contract: Runtime effects are selected by generic facts and shared helpers; display names must not determine behavior.
cases.proposal: If object.display_name equals the invented name Amber Widget, apply the temporary bonus; otherwise skip it even if the same generic facts are present.
cases.evidence: The name comparison is in the runtime effect dispatcher.
cases.reason: The behavior depends directly on a display name, contradicting the specified dispatch boundary.

cases.contract: Runtime behavior is selected from generic facts, without special cases for display names.
cases.proposal: Bind a generic temporary_bonus fact to a shared helper. Both invented objects use that fact despite different names.
cases.evidence: A scenario changes only the display name and gets the same normalized state and event result.
cases.reason: The generic binding and renamed-object check support the narrow name-independent behavior claim.

cases.contract: Replay identity proves reproduction of the recorded transitions. Rule correctness requires a separate expected-outcome scenario.
cases.proposal: Declare the new effect rule-correct because replay bytes match.
cases.evidence: The sole check runs the same implemented transition twice and compares event bytes; no independent expected outcome is supplied.
cases.reason: Reproducing an implementation does not establish the independent correctness requirement.

cases.contract: Replay identity supports reproducibility, while a separate expected-outcome scenario is needed for a rule-correctness claim.
cases.proposal: Report that reproduction passed and rule correctness remains unverified.
cases.evidence: The recorded transition is replayed with identical event bytes; no expected-outcome scenario exists yet.
cases.reason: The completion statement is limited to the property actually checked.

cases.contract: An unfinished checkpoint branch has unknown outcome. A favorable heuristic score is not a terminal win.
cases.proposal: Count the positive-scored horizon branch as a victory in the summary.
cases.evidence: The branch stopped at its action limit and contains no terminal winner event.
cases.reason: The summary promotes nonterminal heuristic evidence to a result that was never observed.

cases.contract: A fair-play choice must use only information visible to the acting seat, never the opponent's hidden hand or draw order.
cases.proposal: Choose an action using a serialized observation.
cases.evidence: The serialization function and its field list are not supplied; it may be either a seat view or a full checkpoint.
cases.reason: The observation boundary cannot be verified from its name alone.

cases.contract: This fixture intentionally gives no authoritative game rule. Only implementation consistency can be inspected; official game-rule correctness requires separate local authority review.
cases.proposal: An effect settles before the next effect. Determine whether that timing matches the official game's rule.
cases.evidence: Only generic implementation behavior is provided. No official source or independent rule interpretation is part of the fixture.
cases.reason: The requested real-game correctness conclusion is outside the evidence supplied, even if implementation behavior is clear.
